pages.lesson:
LESSON: WORD AND SENTENCE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Word and sentence LISTENING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Word and sentence LISTENING
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do we form LISTENING formation learner should be able to: sounds as they sing rhymes and recite words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending
2. recognize words with similar games with peers e.g. come up with sounds words that rhyme
3. appreciate that syllables form  Learners are guided to identify words words listened to (flip chart, boar

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Word and sentence LISTENING

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Word and sentence LISTENING

Teach
• Focus skill: identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Word and sentence LISTENING.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Word and sentence LISTENING
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we form LISTENING formation learner should be able to: sounds as they sing rhymes and recite words?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
